Create an immense abandoned stone city within a rugged mountain valley. Wind a fast-flowing pale turquoise river through it, separating dense ruined districts on both banks, and join the banks with a narrow arched stone bridge. Organically arrange dozens upon dozens of roofless medieval buildings beside narrow dirt lanes, irregular courtyards, and stepped rocky ground. Cluster buildings most tightly beside the river, reducing their density toward the surrounding slopes.

Use weathered gray masonry throughout the architecture. Include squat rectangular houses, taller blocky halls, broken towers, and several larger Gothic structures featuring pointed and rounded arches, arcades, buttress-like wall sections, and partially collapsed upper stories. Leave most buildings with only jagged exterior walls and exposed room divisions; give a few decayed timber frames, beams, balconies, or skeletal roofs. Disperse stairs, retaining walls, rubble piles, fallen logs, and isolated masonry fragments among these ruins.

Make the uneven brown ground interrupted by broad rock shelves, cliffs, large pale boulders, gullies, and steep ridges enclosing the valley. Across open spaces and settlement edges, distribute irregular clusters of mature leafy trees, sparse woodland, scrub, grasses, weeds, and small wildflowers. Preserve a few broad bare courtyards within the denser blocks. Extend rocky, lightly forested mountains beyond the city, threading low white clouds and mist between slopes and buildings.

Keep this sprawling city tightly packed and distinctly unordered. Fit the architecture to natural rock rather than imposing a grid. Apply soft daylight and maintain a quiet, hazy, overgrown atmosphere.
